subject: Recap + pricing ask: hosted API token forecast & peak TPS
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@planetpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + pricing ask: hosted API token forecast & peak TPS

Hi Emily — great to meet earlier. Quick recap of what we agreed and two asks so that I can put a firm hosted pricing illustration together: 

Summary from the call:
- Primary use case: payment confirmation assistant + transactional summarization for customer support. Mixed chat + short completions (~average request ~180 tokens input + 60 tokens output).
- Expected ramp: pilot (1 month) -> scale to prod in ~3 months.
- Success metrics: 95th pct latency under 200ms for user-facing completions, error rate <1%.

Asks (so we can give a concrete $/1M tokens banding):
1) Expected steady-state monthly token consumption (best guess range is fine) — e.g., 5M, 20M, 100M tokens/month.
2) Peak TPS requirement (TPS = tokens per second at burst) — what single-minute peak would you expect?
3) Target unit economics or budget range in $/1M tokens you are aiming for (helps us propose tiered pricing).

What I'll provide after you reply: a hosted pricing illustration showing nominal, peak, and committed-billing bands plus an M.A.P. (attached) with milestone dates and pilot success criteria. I attached our current hosted pricing sheet for reference.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-pricing-v3.pdf (pricing bands), mutual-action-plan-planetpay.xlsx (MAP stub)

Next steps I propose: you reply with quick estimates for 1–3 above; we align on MAP milestones; Redwood will push a pilot quote and a 30-day trial capacity for validation.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@planetpay.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karan Mehta <karan.mehta@planetpay.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + pricing ask: hosted API token forecast & peak TPS

Diego — thanks for the clear recap. Couple quick answers from our side (estimations for now):

1) Expected monthly tokens (steady-state): 12,000,000 tokens/month (this assumes ~200k end-user interactions/day at ~60 tokens consumed per interaction on average after caching). We expect pilot to be ~1.2M tokens for the first month.
2) Peak TPS: we saw in our sim that during marketing spikes we hit ~2.5 TPS (tokens/sec) sustained for a few minutes; absolute single-minute peak could be as high as 3.0 TPS.
3) Budget / target unit economics: we'd like to keep unit cost around $900 per 1M tokens if possible; the business can stretch to $1,200/1M for guaranteed low-latency SLA during promo periods.

Two clarifying Qs: does your hosted pricing include prefix/KV caching by default? And do the quoted bands include streaming vs non-streaming differences?

Best — Emily
Emily Zhao
Head of Product, Conversational AI | PlanetPay
emily.zhao@planetpay.com
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@planetpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + pricing ask: hosted API token forecast & peak TPS

Emily — perfect, this is exactly the level we needed, thank you. Below is a short hosted pricing sketch tailored to the ranges you provided and answers to your two questions.

Hosted pricing sketch (illustrative, final quote in HubSpot):
- Pilot (1 month, test): 1.2M tokens — flat fee + overage at $1,100 / 1M tokens if usage exceeds pilot allotment.
- Steady state (12M tokens/month): we can offer tiered bands. Examples:
  - On-demand (no commit): $1,250 / 1M tokens.
  - Committed (6–12 month commit): $950 / 1M tokens at 12M commitment/month.
  - SLAs & priority: +20% over committed pricing for 99.95% latency SLO and added regional redundancy.
- Peak/Bursting: short 5–10 minute bursts up to ~3 TPS we can absorb within hosted capacity; sustained multi-hour peaks require a predetermined burst allocation (we can include a burst pool in the MAP).

About your questions:
- Caching: yes — prefix/KV caching and automatic KV cache reuse are part of our hosted runtime; effective cache hit-rate will materially reduce billable tokens for repeated prompts. We will instrument a cache-hit projection once we see a sample traffic set.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: our billing model charges per output token regardless of streaming vs non-streaming; streaming has no additional token surcharge, but OS-level concurrency and latency SLOs are managed differently (we'll note this in the quote).

Example unit economics at your steady-state (12M tokens/month) assuming the committed price $950/1M:
- Monthly charge = 12 * $950 = $11,400
- Effective cost per interaction (if avg 60 tokens consumed) = ~$0.057 per interaction

I'll put these numbers into HubSpot and draft a formal pilot quote + MAP (link below). If this looks reasonable, can we lock a pilot start date for the week of 4/26? That gives our infra team a 10 business day lead to reserve hosted capacity.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/987654321/PP-2024-089
DocuSign pricing sheet (draft): https://www.docusign.com/link/pricing-sheet-pp-089

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + pricing ask: hosted API token forecast & peak TPS

Diego / Jonas — quick technical note for the MAP and pilot run:

- Feasibility: 12M tokens/month steady state and 3 TPS single-minute peak are comfortably within our hosted capacity on a single-region footprint. We recommend configuring a short-duration burst pool that can be consumed during promo spikes to avoid throttling.
- Test plan recommendation: 7-day soak that intentionally generates the 3 TPS peak for 10–15 minute windows twice/day to validate latency SLOs and cache-hit assumptions. We'll provide a minimal test harness and a sample traffic file that mirrors the 180 token input / 60 token output distribution Emily described.

I'll attach a short technical checklist for the pilot to the MAP before we send the final DocuSign.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
